The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team** is widely considered the most important squad in the history of the program. It was the season that broke the "NCAA Tournament drought" that had lasted since the school's founding in 1636, marking the transition of Harvard basketball from an Ivy League also-ran to a national contender.

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of everything regarding that historic team.

### 1. Season Overview & Records
*   **Overall Record:** 26–5
*   **Ivy League Record:** 14–0 (Perfect Conference Record)
*   **Postseason:** NCAA Tournament (Round of 64)
*   **Head Coach:** Tommy Amaker (5th season at Harvard)
*   **Home Arena:** Lavietes Pavilion (Boston, Massachusetts)
*   **Final AP Poll Status:** Received votes (finished the season ranked in the "Others Receiving Votes" category).

### 2. Historical Significance
*   **First NCAA Bid:** This was the first time in the 376-year history of the university that the men's basketball team qualified for the NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament.
*   **Ending the Drought:** Prior to this, Harvard's only post-season appearances were in 1946 (NAIA) and the 2011 NIT. This season validated Coach Tommy Amaker's rebuilding project.
*   **Ivy Dominance:** Going 14–0 in the Ivy League was a rare feat, showcasing total dominance over their conference rivals (Yale, Princeton, Cornell, etc.).

### 3. Key Personnel

#### Head Coach: Tommy Amaker
*   Amaker, a former Duke player and Michigan/Harvard coach, was hired to elevate the program's profile.
*   This season was the culmination of his recruiting classes. He was named the **Hugh Durham Award Winner** (mid-major Coach of the Year) and the **Ivy League Coach of the Year**.

#### The Starters & Key Rotation
The team was known for being veteran-heavy, physical, and disciplined.

*   **Keith Wright (Senior, Forward):**
    *   The undisputed leader and star of the team.
    *   **Accolades:** Ivy League Player of the Year (for the second consecutive season), First-Team All-Ivy, NABC District 1 Player of the Year.
    *   **Stats:** Averaged a double-double for the season (approx. 14.2 points, 10.3 rebounds). He was the anchor of the offense and defense.
*   **Laurent Rivard (Senior, Guard):**
    *   The primary outside shooter and clutch performer.
    *   **Accolades:** Second-Team All-Ivy.
    *   **Role:** Known for hitting critical three-pointers to close out games.
*   **Brandyn Curry (Senior, Guard):**
    *   The floor general and defensive stopper.
    *   **Accolades:** First-Team All-Ivy (often recognized for defense).
    *   **Role:** Led the team in assists and steals; guarded the opponent's best perimeter player.
*   **Kyle Casey (Junior, Forward):**
    *   A versatile, athletic forward who could score inside and out.
    *   **Accolades:** Second-Team All-Ivy.
    *   **Note:** Casey was a vital part of the regular season but was **suspended for the NCAA Tournament** due to an off-court altercation at a bar in Cambridge shortly before the tournament.
*   **Oliver McNally (Senior, Forward):**
    *   A stretch-four who could shoot from the perimeter.
    *   **Role:** His importance skyrocketed in the NCAA Tournament when he had to start in place of the suspended Casey.

### 4. Season Narrative & Highlights

#### Non-Conference Success
To secure an at-large bid (since the Ivy League does not have a conference tournament), Harvard needed a strong RPI. They achieved this by beating **Boston College** (an ACC team) 78–70 in December. This was a marquee non-conference win that proved they could compete with high-major programs. They also defeated Providence and UMass during the season.

#### The Ivy League Run
Harvard opened conference play with a win and never looked back.
*   They swept their biggest rival, **Yale**, which was crucial for the league title.
*   They clinched the Ivy League title and the NCAA bid on **March 3, 2012**, with a win over Cornell in front of a raucous Lavietes Pavilion crowd.
*   The 14–0 record was the first perfect conference season in Harvard history.

### 5. The NCAA Tournament Run
*   **Seed:** Harvard was awarded a **No. 12 seed** in the South Region.
*   **Opponent:** They faced the **No. 5 seed Vanderbilt Commodores** (led by star guard John Jenkins).
*   **The Game:** Played in Nashville, TN (Vanderbilt's home region).
*   **The Result:** Harvard lost **71–59**.
*   **The Performance:** Despite the loss, Harvard competed respectably. They kept the game close into the second half. Keith Wright fought through foul trouble to score 18 points and grab 10 rebounds. Laurent Rivard scored 14 points.
*   **The Aftermath:** While a first-round exit, simply playing in the "Big Dance" was celebrated as a monumental victory on campus. The team received a hero's welcome back in Cambridge.

### 6. Statistical Profile
*   **Defense:** The team was stingy, holding opponents to low shooting percentages, anchored by Wright's rim protection and Curry's perimeter pressure.
*   **Efficiency:** They played a slow, deliberate pace (typical of Ivy League basketball at the time) but were highly efficient on offense, rarely turning the ball over.
*   **Rebounding:** They dominated the glass, largely due to Wright and Casey, often out-rebounding taller teams.

### 7. Awards and Honors
*   **Keith Wright:** Ivy League Player of the Year; NABC All-District 1 First Team.
*   **Tommy Amaker:** Ivy League Coach of the Year; Hugh Durham Award (National Mid-Major Coach of the Year).
*   **All-Ivy First Team:** Keith Wright, Brandyn Curry.
*   **All-Ivy Second Team:** Kyle Casey, Laurent Rivard.
*   **All-Ivy Honorable Mention:** Oliver McNally.

### 8. Legacy and Impact
The 2011–12 team changed the trajectory of Harvard basketball permanently.
*   **The "Harvard Era":** This team opened the door for three more consecutive NCAA Tournament appearances (2013, 2014, 2015).
*   **Recruiting:** It proved that high-academic institutions could compete athletically, helping Amaker recruit better talent in subsequent years (leading to players like Siyani Chambers, Wesley Saunders, and Zena Edosomwan).
*   **National Perception:** It forced the national media to take the Ivy League seriously again.
*   **Keith Wright's Legacy:** Wright is often cited as the greatest player in Harvard history, and this season was his crowning achievement.

### Summary
The 2011–12 Harvard Crimson were not just a "Cinderella story"; they were a well-oiled machine of seniors who had been developing together for four years. They combined academic excellence with high-level Division I basketball, culminating in the program's first-ever NCAA Tournament berth. While their tournament run was short, their regular-season dominance and historical breakthrough make them the most significant team in Harvard basketball history.
